- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction to pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate mean reversion toward sentiment pivot point.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; use 14-day moving average of history as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and price is trending, model often lags; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to capture momentum.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 14-day low if sentiment is positive — model tends to underestimate recovery in bullish phases.
